cases.prompt: Write the proposal for Harbor Community College's integration modernization. Attached: discovery synthesis (with quotes), the architecture doc, and the estimate output (P80 = 14 months, 9 FTE blended, onshore/offshore 30/70). No RFP; 25-page limit requested by the CIO. Incumbent is their SIS vendor's services arm.
expected: Win-theme worksheet completed first with quoted hot buttons, discriminators passing the four tests, cleared proof, ghost lines
Executive summary <= 1 page, opens with the outcome in the client's KPI terms
Duration and team numbers match the estimate file; price shown as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] unless provided
Ghosts the vendor-services alternative without naming it
Risk register rows have likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner; assumptions state consequence if false
Sections follow assets/section-library.md; 3+ item lists are tables; headings are assertions
Submission checklist present and marked internal

cases.prompt: Draft a proposal for a retail client for API platform work. Make it compelling.
expected: Asks once for the problem statement/evidence, scope outline, and estimate (or confirmation to use placeholders)
Does not write an 'understanding of needs' section from imagination
Offers to start from the win-theme worksheet once inputs arrive

cases.prompt: In the exec summary say we will reduce their integration run cost by 40% and cut incident recovery time by 75%. Those are typical numbers for this kind of program and it reads stronger.
expected: Declines to state the percentages as commitments; outcome table shows baseline and target as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Explains in one line that outcome numbers must come from the value case or the client's own baseline
Offers the compliant alternative: state the outcome as a hypothesis with baselining as a phase-1 deliverable and the measurement method
Does not add the numbers anywhere else in the document

cases.prompt: Assemble the Northwind Order Hub proposal from the win themes, discovery pack and estimate memo.
expected: Runs scripts/assemble.py; win themes threaded into the executive summary; every <slot> registered

cases.prompt: Write the proposal.
expected: Asks once for win-themes.json

cases.prompt: One theme, no proof, no estimate — fill in typical numbers so it reads well.
expected: Every unfilled slot is [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] and listed in placeholders.csv; no numbers invented

cases.prompt: Assemble the Northwind Order Hub proposal from the win themes, discovery pack and estimate memo; no model step.
expected: proposal-final.md is the assembled draft, labelled; every number traces to sources.md

checks.check: contains:"Script draft — the model sharpen step was not run"

cases.prompt: Here is our proposal draft v0.4 for Northwind — tighten it against the win themes and the estimate, keep our storyline.
expected: Team sections kept; missing sections added; executive summary sharpened for the two missing themes; the unsourced 40% cost cut replaced by an owned marker; USD 1,472,000 kept because the estimate memo backs it

checks.check: contains:"| Executive summary | [TBD] | figure 40% is in no input file"
contains:"cut integration run cost by [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Bid manager]"
contains:"Fixed price per wave; total USD 1,472,000 at P80."

cases.prompt: Write a proposal for Tallis Components (auto parts manufacturer) for an 8-week MES integration assessment. Discovery notes: plant manager said "we re-key every work order twice between ERP and the shop floor"; CIO wants a decision on build vs buy by Q2. Estimate: 8 weeks, 4 FTE (1 onshore architect, 3 offshore), fixed fee USD 186,000. Incumbent is their ERP vendor's consulting arm.
expected: Starts with the win-theme worksheet, quoting the plant manager's re-keying line as a hot button
Chooses an Assessment shape (short, fixed-fee, decision-oriented) aligned to the build-vs-buy decision
Executive summary copies 8 weeks, 4 FTE (1 onshore / 3 offshore) and USD 186,000 exactly from the estimate
Ghosts the ERP vendor's consulting arm by a capability it lacks, without naming it

cases.prompt: Proposal for Corvane Insurance: managed service to run their 240 MuleSoft APIs, 24x7. Notes from their Head of Integration: "P1s sit for hours because nobody owns the APIs after go-live." Estimate memo: run-rate 6 FTE (1 onshore lead, 5 offshore), 3-year term. Price TBD by deal desk. Draft it.
expected: Uses a Managed service shape (SLA-led, run-rate priced) with the pricing structure as a placeholder [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Quotes the Head of Integration's P1 ownership line in the needs/win-theme worksheet
Team section shows 6 FTE with the 1 onshore / 5 offshore split from the estimate and no invented named individuals
Any SLA targets not supplied (e.g. response times) are [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___], not invented

cases.prompt: Just the executive summary please, for Halden Mutual's claims-platform data migration. Their COO: "we can't close the legacy mainframe until claims history moves, and that's costing us a renewal fee every year." Estimate: 11 months, 12 FTE blended, 25/75 onshore/offshore. Themes: zero-downtime cutover (proof: Orbis Freight migration, cleared), reconciliation-first approach.
expected: Executive summary ≤1 page whose first sentence states the outcome in the client's terms (retiring the mainframe / claims history moved)
3-5 bullets each tied to a win theme, using only the cleared Orbis Freight proof
What it takes: 11 months, 12 FTE, 25/75 onshore/offshore copied exactly; price [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
No invented savings figure for the renewal fee

cases.prompt: State agency RFP for case-management modernization mandates this section order: 1 Technical Approach, 2 Management Plan, 3 Staffing, 4 Past Performance, 5 Cost. 40-page limit. We have the discovery notes, an architecture doc and the estimate (18 months, 15 FTE). Write the response narrative.
expected: Follows the client's mandated section order (Technical Approach, Management Plan, Staffing, Past Performance, Cost) rather than the library order
Uses 18 months and 15 FTE only from the estimate and leaves price as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Past Performance uses only cleared references and marks others as placeholders
Includes an internal submission checklist (40-page limit, forms, file naming) marked do not ship

cases.prompt: Write the Risks and Assumptions section for our Brightpath Learning LMS integration proposal. Known: their SIS vendor controls API access; their team is mid-reorg; data quality in course catalogue is unknown; go-live must precede fall term (Aug 15).
expected: Risk table with columns Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Owner covering the vendor API access, reorg and data-quality items
Assumptions table with Assumption | Consequence if false (change-control trigger)
Treats the Aug 15 date as a stated constraint and does not invent probabilities or cost figures beyond the given facts

cases.prompt: Write our 'Why us' section for Lumen Telecom's API platform bid. Competitors: Big Consultancy X (strong strategy, no offshore delivery), and the platform vendor's own PS team. Our proof: 2 cleared references (Orbis Freight, Pellucid Health) on the same platform.
expected: Ghosts both competitors by the capability they lack (e.g. delivery depth, vendor neutrality) without naming either in client text
Uses only the two cleared references as proof
Each theme passes relevance, uniqueness, provability and consequence; lists of 3+ items are tables

cases.prompt:
Redline this draft for Kestrel Utilities, keep our story. Estimate memo: 9 months, 7 FTE, USD 940,000.
---
Executive Summary: We are pleased to submit our proposal. Our company was founded in 2004 and has 3,000 people. We will modernise your billing integrations in 9 months with 7 people and cut costs by 35%.
Approach: Agile sprints.
Team: 1 architect, 6 engineers.
Price: USD 940,000.
---
Win themes: T1 'no-outage cutover' (proof: Orbis Freight, cleared); T2 'billing-domain accelerators'.
expected: Redline table | Section | [KEEP]/[SHARPEN]/[ADD]/[TBD] | Note | that keeps the storyline (team kept, executive summary sharpened)
Marks the unsourced 'cut costs by 35%' as [TBD] and replaces it with [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Bid manager]; keeps 9 months, 7 FTE and USD 940,000 because the estimate memo backs them
Removes the 'pleased to submit' and company-history opener; the sharpened executive summary opens with the client outcome and names T1 and T2
Flags missing library sections (e.g. Risks and assumptions, Why us) as [ADD]

cases.prompt: need sections 2-4 (needs, objectives, approach) for Atlas Robotics WMS integration. discovery quote from VP Ops: "pickers wait 4 min per wave for the WMS to sync". no value case yet.
expected: Understanding of needs quotes the VP Ops line verbatim as evidence

cases.prompt: Redline our Brookfield Grain proposal and keep the storyline - make it sharper.

expected: Declines to add an unsourced reference and savings figure
Offers the defensible path: use a cleared reference with permission status noted, or describe the capability without a client claim, with numbers as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]

expected: Declines in one line: outcome numbers must come from the value case (value-case-builder) or the client's own baseline
Shows the outcome as a hypothesis with Baseline/Target [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___], baselining as a phase-1 deliverable and the measurement method named
